Likutay Halachos

Yoreh Daya

Hilchos Nedarim 5

☰ Hebrew – Introduction

Based on the Torah "Rabbi Shimon opened…" etc. [Likutay Moharan I, Torah 60] — see there the entire Torah. It is explained there that through sipuray ma'asiyos [stories/tales], those who are sleeping are awakened from their sleep. For there are people who sleep away their days, G-d forbid — that is, they fall into a deep sleep, and their mochin [consciousness/mentality] and their da'as [awareness] sleep, and they do not know at all of the greatness of Hashem and of the ultimate purpose for which the world was created. And the primary way to awaken them from this sleep is through sipuray ma'asiyos — stories of the deeds and the greatness of Hashem and of the tzadikim.

And through this awakening from sleep, one merits pekidos akaros [the visitation/remembrance of the barren] — that barren women are visited and give birth. And one merits redemption from all exiles. For all the exiles are aspects of sleep, and when one is awakened from sleep, one goes out from exile to redemption. And all this is the aspect of nedarim, as will be explained.

☰ Hebrew § 1

And this is the aspect of nedarim — that a person can forbid upon himself a permitted thing, or obligate himself to do a voluntary matter, through a neder or shevuah. For through the neder and the shevuah, a person reveals and arouses the holiness that is hidden and sleeping within the thing. For in every thing in the world there is concealed holiness, concealed Torah — and through the neder he awakens this sleeping holiness and reveals it. And then it becomes Torah — a mitzvah and avayrah — that which previously had no prohibition or obligation.

And this is precisely the aspect of awakening from sleep, for the holiness that was sleeping within the thing is now awakened and revealed through the neder. And this is the power of the neder — to awaken the sleeping holiness within all things and to draw it into revelation.

☰ Hebrew § 2

And this itself is the aspect of nedarim, which are drawn from a very lofty place, as is known — from the aspect of the concealed Torah. Through this one can awaken the dormant holiness in all things, for the concealed Torah is the root of all holiness that is hidden in all things in the world. And this is the aspect of awakening from sleep — that through the concealed Torah, which is the aspect of nedarim, one awakens all the dormant holiness. And this is the aspect of what is explained in the aforementioned T see there. And therefore Chanah, when she asked Hashem for a child, she made a neder, as it is written, "And she vowed a vow and said: Hashem of Hosts, if You will indeed look upon the affliction of Your maidservant…" (I Samuel 1:11) etc. For through the neder, which is the aspect of awakening from sleep — through this one merits pekidos akaros. For the barrenness is an aspect of sleep and dormancy — the flow of life is asleep and dormant, and the womb does not produce fruit. And through the neder, which awakens the dormant holiness, the flow of life is awakened, and the barren one is visited.

And this is why Chanah specifically made a neder when praying for a child — because the neder is the mechanism for awakening what is dormant, and barrenness is itself the aspect of dormancy. And through the neder she drew down the power to awaken the flow of life and to bring forth the child — Shemu'ail HaNavi, peace be upon him.

☰ Hebrew § 4

And this is the aspect of Pesach. For the primary redemption from Egypt — which includes all the exiles — is through the aspect of the aforementioned awakening from sleep. For all the exiles are aspects of sleep, as mentioned above, and the primary redemption is through awakening from sleep. And this is the aspect of what is said regarding the redemption from Egypt: "I was asleep but my heart was awake" (Song of Songs 5:2) — for even in the midst of the exile, which is sleep, the heart — the inner point of holiness — was awake. And through awakening this point, the entire redemption came.

And the Pesach offering itself alludes to this, for Pesach is the aspect of peh sach [the mouth that speaks/tells] — the aspect of sipuray ma'asiyos, through which one awakens from sleep, as mentioned above. And through this the redemption from Egypt was accomplished, and through this all future redemptions will be accomplished.

☰ Hebrew § 5

But there are those who awaken from sleep through sipuray ma'asiyos, which are in the aspect of "in the midst of years" [b'kerev shanim], the aspect of "the days of seventy years" [shivim shanah] — seventy [years of] sleep. For there are those who are so deeply sunk in sleep — in the aspect of the seventy years of sleep — that they cannot be awakened through ordinary means. And for them, the sipuray ma'asiyos are needed — that is, the stories of the ancient years, the stories of the great deeds of Hashem from long ago, the stories of the tzadikim of earlier generations. And through these stories they are awakened even from the deepest sleep.

And this is the aspect of the stories that our Rebbe of blessed memory told — the Sipuray Ma'asiyos [the Thirteen Tales] — which have the power to awaken even those in the deepest sleep, in the deepest exile. For these stories are drawn from the very highest places, from the concealed Torah, from before creation — and they have the power to reach down even to the lowest depths and awaken the dormant holiness there.

☰ Hebrew § 6

segments.he: הרב חייב למול את עבדו. ואחר כך חייב במצות שהאשה חייבת בהם. כי העבד הוא קנין כספו והוא ממונו של האדון וכל הנפשות שרשם בעשירות כמובא בדברי רבינו נ"י (בסי' ס"ט) וע"כ כשקונה עבד ונעשה ממונו. נמצא שהוא בחי' שורש נפשו והנפש הוא בחי' מלכות דקודשה. והעבד הוא ההיפך ממלכות דקדושה בבח'י תחת עבד כי ימלוך. כי העבד הוא זוהמת הנחש בבחי' ארור כנען וכו' בי' אור אתה וכו' כמובא. והוא בחי' מלכות הרשעה שהוא בחי' הנחש שהוא ההיפךממלכות דקדושה. וע"כ כשהעבד בא לרשות ישראל להיות ממונו של ישראל צריך למולו להכניע הערלה שהיא רע הכולל שהוא זוהמת הנחש שהוא מלכות הרשעה. כדי שיהי' נכנע תחת יד ישראל להיות ממונו של ישראל. דהיינו בחי' נפשו של ישראל שהוא בחי' מלכות דקדושה כנ"ל:
segments.en:
And this is the aspect of the mitzvah of telling the story of the Exodus [sipur yetzias Mitzrayim], the aspect of "whoever elaborates in telling the story of the Exodus is praiseworthy." For through the telling of the story of the Exodus, one draws upon oneself the aspect of the awakening from sleep that was accomplished at the time of the Exodus. For the telling of the story is itself the mechanism of awakening — the sipuray ma'asiyos that awaken from sleep. And therefore whoever elaborates in telling is praiseworthy — for the more one tells, the more one awakens, and the greater the redemption that is drawn down.

And through this telling, the neder is activated — for the telling reveals the concealed Torah that is hidden within the events of the Exodus. And through this revelation, new holiness is drawn into the world, new mitzvos are created, and the dormant holiness in all things is awakened. And this is why the night of Pesach — the seder night — is the primary time for telling the story, for it is the night when the great awakening from sleep took place.

☰ Hebrew § 7

For the primary telling of the Exodus and of all the miracles and wonders that Hashem does with us in every generation, in every year, and at every time — it must be specifically to Hashem. That is, the telling must be directed toward Hashem Himself — not merely as a recounting of historical events, but as a declaration of His greatness and His wonders directed to Him. And this is the aspect of prayer — for the telling of the wonders of Hashem is itself prayer. And through this prayer-telling, one awakens the dormant holiness and draws the redemption.

And this is the aspect of "Hashem, Your work — in the midst of years, give it life" (Habakkuk 3:2) — that through telling of "Your work" — Hashem's deeds and wonders — to Hashem Himself, one draws life even in the midst of the years of sleep and exile. And through this, the awakening spreads to all, and the dormant holiness in all things is brought to life.

☰ Hebrew § 8

And this is "Great are the works of Hashem" (Psalms 111:2) etc. — the aspect of the aforementioned sipuray ma'asiyos. "Splendor and majesty are His work" — the aspect of "Hashem, Your work" mentioned above, from which is drawn the aspect of hod [splendor] and hadar [majesty]. For through the telling of the great deeds of Hashem, the kavod and the hadar of Hashem are revealed in the world. And this is the ultimate purpose — that through the sipuray ma'asiyos and through the nedarim that awaken the dormant holiness, the splendor and majesty of Hashem's kingship should be revealed throughout all the earth.

And this connects to what is explained in the aforementioned Torah regarding the aspect of zahav [gold] — that through the awakening from sleep, one merits true wealth, which is the aspect of da'as [knowledge/awareness]. For sleep is the absence of da'as, and awakening is the restoration of da'as. And true wealth is da'as — the awareness and recognition of the greatness of Hashem.

☰ Hebrew § 9

And this is "You were sold for nothing, and not with money shall you be redeemed" (Isaiah 52:3) — but rather from the aspect of zahav [gold], as is found in the kavanos of Pesach in Pri Aitz Chaim. For the redemption is not through silver — which is the aspect of chesed and the revealed Torah — but through zahav, which is the aspect of gevurah and the concealed Torah, the aspect of Binah. For the exile is so deep — the sleep is so profound — that only the concealed Torah, which is drawn from the very highest places, has the power to reach down and awaken and redeem.

And this is the aspect of nedarim, which are in Binah, in the aspect of zahav — through which the redemption comes. And this is why the redemption from Egypt specifically involved the gold that Israel took from Egypt — for through this gold, which is the aspect of the concealed Torah drawn into revelation, the redemption was accomplished. And through this aspect of zahav, all future redemptions will be accomplished as well.

☰ Hebrew § 10

All the wealth of the entire world is drawn only from the tzadik, for only he merits true wealth — through which one attains the hisbonenus [contemplation] to contemplate and recognize the greatness of Hashem from all things in the world. For the true wealth is the da'as to see His G-dliness in everything — and this is drawn only through the tzadik.

And therefore, even material wealth — the physical gold and silver of this world — is ultimately drawn through the tzadik. For the physical wealth is a garment and a vessel for the spiritual wealth, which is the da'as and the hisbonenus. And when the spiritual source flows through the tzadik, the physical bounty flows with it. And therefore one must connect oneself to the true tzadik — for through him, both spiritual and material abundance flows to all the world.

And this is the aspect of nedarim — for through the neder, which draws from the concealed Torah through the tzadik, one draws both spiritual awakening and material abundance into the world. And this is the connection between nedarim, sipuray ma'asiyos, awakening from sleep, pekidos akaros, the redemption from Egypt, and true wealth — they are all one unified concept, all flowing from the concealed Torah, all accomplished through the true tzadik. Blessed be Hashem forever, Amen and Amen.

Translator's Summary

This halacha, based on Likutay Moharan I, Torah 60 ("Pasach Rabbi Shimon"), centers on the concept of awakening from spiritual sleep — and reveals nedarim as the mechanism of that awakening.

Core Teaching: All things in the world contain dormant, concealed holiness (= concealed Torah). A neder awakens this sleeping holiness, bringing it into revelation — creating new Torah (mitzvah and avayrah) from what was previously neutral. This is precisely the dynamic of "sipuray ma'asiyos" (stories) that awaken those who sleep — for to tell the story of Hashem's deeds is to reveal the concealed holiness within the events of the world.

Key Connections:

Nedarim = Awakening from sleep — The neder reveals the concealed Torah hidden within things, just as stories awaken the sleeping consciousness.

Chanah's vow — She vowed a neder when praying for a child, because nedarim (awakening) lead to pekidos akaros (visitation of the barren). Barrenness = dormancy; the neder awakens the dormant flow of life.

Pesach = Peh Sach — The mouth that tells/speaks — the sipuray ma'asiyos of the Exodus that awaken Israel from the sleep of exile. "Whoever elaborates in telling the Exodus is praiseworthy" — for more telling = more awakening = greater redemption.

Zahav (Gold) = Binah = Concealed Torah = Nedarim — "Not with silver shall you be redeemed" but with gold — redemption comes through the concealed Torah (Binah), not the revealed. This is also the root of true wealth: da'as/awareness, drawn through the tzadik.

The Tzadik as Source: All wealth — spiritual and material — flows through the tzadik who connects the concealed Torah to revelation. Nedarim, stories, awakening, fertility, redemption, and wealth are all one concept flowing through this single channel.
